mainTopic: A man going out on שבת with weapons, and the אגדות that grow out of it about ימות המשיח, Torah study, and kindness
overview: The amud opens by finishing an אגדה about ירושלים. רב חסדא explains that the people's coded questions were all hints about immorality. Then רבי יהודה describes the city's fragrant cinnamon firewood, hidden away after the חורבן. A new משנה rules that a man may not go out on שבת with weapons, while רבי אליעזר says weapons are a man's תכשיטין and the חכמים say they are a disgrace. The גמרא brings two versions of a ברייתא about whether weapons will disappear in ימות המשיח, and ties each version to the views of שמואל and רבי חייא בר אבא. רבי אליעזר's source is the פסוק 'gird your sword… your glory', defended with the rule אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו and רב כהנא's lesson to first learn and then understand. A series of teachings from רבי אלעזר and ריש לקיש then praises scholars who learn together properly, adds rewards for doing מצוות, and ranks loans and partnership above צדקה. The amud ends in the middle of ריש לקיש's teaching about a vicious dog keeping חסד out of a home, and the פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last coded questions the people of ירושלים asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a list of questions the people of ירושלים used to ask each other, which sound like questions about food and company.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did you drink dark wine? Did you sit on a wide couch or a narrow couch? Were you with a good friend or a bad friend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started on the previous page: questions the people of ירושלים would ask one another. They look innocent here, but the next line will show they meant something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the list included questions like 'Did you eat well-kneaded bread or not?' and 'White wine?' This passage adds the last items: dark wine, a wide or narrow couch, and a good or bad friend. On the surface these are everyday questions about a meal.

keyTerms.meaning: A couch or divan people reclined on while eating

steps.confusionAlert: These are not really questions about food or furniture. רב חסדא explains in the next step that they are code words.

phrases.english: With dark (mustard-colored) wine?
phrases.notes: Continues the earlier question about white wine versus dark wine.

phrases.english: On a wide couch, or on a narrow couch?
With a good companion, or with a bad companion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list that began on the previous daf, on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of ירושלים asked each other questions about wine, couches, and companions.

steps.title: רב חסדא decodes the questions as hints about women
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that all of these questions were really about women and immorality.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: All of these questions are about immorality.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tells us what the questions really meant. They were all hidden references to women and immoral behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is a code word. Well-kneaded bread means a woman who is not a virgin. White or dark wine means a fair or dark-complexioned woman. A wide or narrow couch means a heavy or thin woman. A good friend means a good-looking woman. This shows how coarse the talk in ירושלים had become.
steps.whatToRemember: The questions about food and couches were all code. רב חסדא says they all refer to זנות.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
And all of them refer to promiscuity.
phrases.notes: Each of those questions was a polite, hidden way of describing a kind of woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the hidden meaning of the questions in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the questions were euphemisms for immorality.

steps.title: The cinnamon firewood of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה teaches that the firewood of ירושלים was cinnamon wood, and that it was hidden away after the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said in the name of רבי יהודה: The wood of ירושלים was cinnamon wood. When they burned it, its smell spread through all of ארץ ישראל. Once ירושלים was destroyed, the wood was hidden away. Only a piece the size of a barley grain was left, and it is found in the treasury of Queen צימצמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another story about ירושלים. This one describes how special the city was before the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous lines showed the low behavior in ירושלים. This line shows how great the city once was: even its ordinary fuel was precious cinnamon. After the חורבן that greatness was hidden, and only a tiny remnant is left.

phrases.english: Rachava said that Rabbi Yehuda said:
The wood (fuel logs) of Jerusalem was cinnamon wood,
and when they would burn them,
their scent spread through all of the Land of Israel.
And once Jerusalem was destroyed, they were hidden away,
and nothing remained except a piece the size of a barley grain,
and it is found in the treasury of Queen Tzimtzemai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה about ירושלים, connected to the previous one only by topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The firewood of ירושלים was fragrant cinnamon wood, hidden away after the חורבן except for a barley-sized piece.

steps.title: A man may not go out on שבת with weapons
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a man may not go out on שבת with weapons, and if he does he must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man may not go out with a sword, a bow, a shield, a club, or a spear. If he did go out with one, he must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. Earlier in the chapter we learned which items a woman may wear outside on שבת. Now the משנה turns to a man and his weapons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing real clothing or jewelry outside on שבת is allowed, but carrying an object into the public domain is forbidden. The תנא קמא holds that weapons are just objects being carried, not clothing or jewelry. That is why someone who goes out with them by mistake is חייב חטאת, the offering brought for breaking שבת unintentionally.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
Sin-offering, brought for breaking שבת by mistake

steps.whyThisMatters: The question is whether weapons count as a man's 'clothing and jewelry' or as a load being carried. That is the debate the next line opens.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A man may not go out with a sword,
nor with a bow, nor with a shield,
nor with a club, nor with a spear.
And if he went out (with one), he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יֵצֵא הָאִישׁ לֹא בְּסַיִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the אגדה before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weapons are a load, not clothing. Going out with them on שבת makes a person חייב חטאת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: weapons are a man's ornaments
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees and holds that weapons count as ornaments for a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: They are ornaments for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He says weapons are like jewelry for a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a man may go out on שבת wearing his ornaments, weapons would be treated the same way. By this view, a man who goes out with weapons is not carrying a load and is not חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says weapons are a load and carrying them makes one חייב חטאת. רבי אליעזר says they are a man's תכשיטין, so it is allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
They are ornaments for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: תַּכְשִׁיטִין הֵן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weapons are ornaments for a man, so going out with them on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: The Sages say weapons are a disgrace, not an ornament
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר. They say weapons are only a disgrace, and they bring a פסוק showing that in the ideal future weapons will be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: weapons are nothing but a disgrace, as the verse says: 'They shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift sword against nation, and they will not learn war anymore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the חכמים's answer to רבי אליעזר. He said weapons are ornaments, and they say weapons are a disgrace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ornament (תכשיט) is something a person is proud to wear, so it may be worn out on שבת. The חכמים say weapons are the opposite: in the perfect future of the נביא, people will melt them down into farm tools. Something that will be thrown away in the ideal world cannot count as an ornament, so wearing it outside on שבת is carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה
For disgrace; something shameful, not something to be proud of
Pruning hooks, tools for trimming vines

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason behind the ruling at the start of the משנה (step 4) that a man who goes out with weapons brings a חטאת. Weapons are not ornaments, so they count as a carried load.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
they are nothing but a disgrace,
as it is said:
"And they shall beat their swords into plowshares
and their spears into pruning hooks;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִשָּׂא גוֹי אֶל גּוֹי חֶרֶב
phrases.english: nation will not lift sword against nation,
and they will not learn war anymore."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to רבי אליעזר in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weapons are a disgrace, not an ornament. A verse about their future destruction supports this.

steps.title: A garter is pure and may be worn out on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה turns to a woman's leg items. A בירית (garter) cannot become טמא, and a woman may go out wearing it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A garter is pure, and one may go out with it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new item, a garter worn on the leg. It rules that the garter is טהור and may be worn outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garter is a band that holds up the stocking. The משנה rules that it cannot become טמא, and the גמרא explains this later. It is permitted on שבת because, as רש״י explains, a woman will not take it off to show it to others, since that would expose her leg.

keyTerms.meaning: A garter, a band on the leg that holds up the stocking
Pure; here it means it cannot become ritually impure

phrases.english: A garter is pure
and one may go out with it on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from men's weapons to a new item, a woman's leg item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בירית cannot become טמא and is permitted to be worn outside on שבת.

steps.title: Ankle chains can become impure and may not be worn out on שבת
steps.stepSummary: In contrast to the garter, כבלים (ankle chains) can become טמא, and a woman may not go out wearing them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ankle chains are susceptible to impurity, and one may not go out with them on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite ruling for a similar leg item. Ankle chains can become טמא and may not be worn outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ankle chains are real ornaments, which is why they can become טמא. Like the other ornaments in this perek, the worry is that a woman might take them off and carry them, so the חכמים forbade wearing them out. The two rulings together teach that leg items are not all the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Ankle chains; ornamental chains worn on the legs

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two items. The בירית (garter) holds up clothing and is permitted. The כבלים (chains) are ornaments and are forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with three rulings: weapons are a disgrace according to the חכמים (חטאת if worn out), a garter is pure and permitted, and ankle chains are susceptible to impurity and forbidden.

phrases.english: Ankle chains are susceptible to impurity
and one may not go out with them on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָלִים — טְמֵאִים וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting case to the garter in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כבלים can become טמא and are forbidden to be worn outside on שבת.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what the word אלה means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. It asks what the word אלה means. This word appeared in the משנה's list of weapons.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is an אלה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking about one unfamiliar word from the משנה. This sets up the short answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed the weapons a man may not go out with: a sword, a bow, a shield, an אלה, and a spear. The word אלה is unclear, so the גמרא first defines it before discussing anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A weapon named in the משנה's list

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'alla'?
phrases.notes: The ב is just copied from the משנה's own words, 'with an alla.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by returning to a word in the weapons list from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אלה in the משנה.

steps.title: An אלה is a club
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an אלה is a קולפא, a club.
steps.simpleTranslation: A club.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. An אלה is a club.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer simply translates the משנה's Hebrew word into the familiar Aramaic word קולפא. Now the whole list of weapons in the משנה is clear.

keyTerms.meaning: A club, a heavy stick used as a weapon

phrases.english: A club.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה where רבי אליעזר says weapons are ornaments for a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: they (the weapons) are ornaments for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words again so it can start discussing them. This is a setup line that prepares the ברייתא coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר holds that a sword or bow counts as jewelry, so a man may wear one in the street on שבת. The גמרא now wants to examine this view more closely using a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Ornaments, jewelry. On שבת you may wear these in the street, because wearing is not carrying.
The תנא who says weapons count as a man's ornaments

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
They are ornaments for him.
phrases.notes: "They" means the weapons listed in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר תַּכְשִׁיטִין הֵן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining אלה as a club, the גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weapons are considered ornaments for a man.

steps.title: The Rabbis ask: if weapons are ornaments, why will they disappear?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the חכמים challenging רבי אליעזר: if weapons are ornaments, why will they be done away with in ימות המשיח?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: They said to רבי אליעזר: Since they are ornaments for him, why will they be eliminated in the days of משיח?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי אליעזר's view. They point out that the נביא promises weapons will be gone in the future, which would make no sense if weapons are beautiful jewelry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody gets rid of jewelry in a perfect world. If weapons disappear in ימות המשיח, that suggests they are a flaw, not an ornament. This supports the חכמים's view that weapons are a גנאי (disgrace).

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה)
The days of משיח, the messianic era

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
Since they are ornaments for him,
why will they be eliminated
in the days of the Messiah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּתַכְשִׁיטִין הֵן לוֹ מִפְּנֵי מָה הֵן בְּטֵלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view just quoted from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that weapons are ornaments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ornaments would not be removed in a perfect future. Since weapons will be removed, they must be a flaw.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers: they will simply not be needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that weapons will disappear only because there will be no more war, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Because they will not be needed, as it says: "Nation will not lift up sword against nation."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends himself. Weapons will not go away because they are ugly. They will go away because nobody will need them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the same פסוק differently. It does not show that weapons are bad. It shows that war will end. So weapons can still be ornaments today.

keyTerms.term: לֹא יִשָּׂא גוֹי אֶל גּוֹי חֶרֶב
keyTerms.meaning: "Nation will not lift sword against nation" (ישעיה ב:ד)

phrases.english: He said to them: Because they will not be needed,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא יִשָּׂא גוֹי אֶל גּוֹי חֶרֶב״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "Nation will not raise sword against nation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason for the removal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weapons disappear because they are a disgrace.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weapons disappear only because they are no longer useful. Their status as ornaments stays.

steps.title: Why not keep weapons just for decoration?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if there is no war, let weapons stay as simple decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them remain just for beauty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אליעזר's answer. If weapons really are jewelry, people should keep wearing them for their looks even when there is no war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jewelry is worn for beauty, not for use. So "not needed" should not be a reason to get rid of an ornament. The question tests whether רבי אליעזר's answer really holds.

phrases.english: And let them be merely for beauty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that weapons disappear because they are not needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ornaments do not need a practical use, so they should remain for beauty.

steps.title: אביי: like a candle at noon
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a weapon without a use is like a candle burning in daylight. It adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is just like a candle in the middle of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. A weapon's beauty comes from its usefulness, so once it is useless it is no longer beautiful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A candle at noon gives no useful light, so it looks pointless rather than nice. A weapon is an ornament because it shows strength for battle. Without war, it loses that value.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like (a comparison formula)

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is just like
a candle at noon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַשְּׁרָגָא בְּטִיהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why weapons cannot stay as decoration.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ornaments are beautiful even without any use.
steps.terutzMaskana: A weapon's beauty depends on its use. Without war it is pointless, like a candle in daylight.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, weapons are ornaments now. They disappear in ימות המשיח only because war ends, and a useless weapon is like a candle at noon.

steps.title: This ברייתא disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this ברייתא disagrees with שמואל. שמואל holds that ימות המשיח differs from today only in that the Jews will no longer be ruled by other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with שמואל. For שמואל said: The only difference between this world and the days of משיח is that the Jews will no longer be subjugated to the nations, as it says: "For the poor will never cease from the land."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and compares the ברייתא to another אמורא's view. The ברייתא says war ends in ימות המשיח, but שמואל holds that the world stays basically the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides in the ברייתא assume weapons will be removed in ימות המשיח, which means war will end. שמואל says the only change is freedom from foreign rule. He proves this from the פסוק saying poor people will always exist, so normal life, including war, continues.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish people being ruled by other nations in exile

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Shmuel.
For Shmuel said:
There is no difference between this world
and the days of the Messiah
except the subjugation of the exiles alone,
as it is said: "For the poor will not cease"
"from within the land."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broader conclusion from the ברייתא's shared assumption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: ימות המשיח differs from today only in ending the Jews' subjugation to other nations.
steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement with שמואל is not between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים. Both of them agree weapons will be removed. It is the ברייתא as a whole that disagrees with שמואל.

steps.title: This ברייתא supports רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports רבי חייא בר אבא, who says all the prophets' promises are about ימות המשיח. Only עולם הבא is beyond description.
steps.simpleTranslation: It supports רבי חייא בר אבא. For רבי חייא בר אבא said: All the prophets prophesied only about the days of משיח, but about עולם הבא it says: "No eye has seen it, God, except You."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which view the ברייתא fits. רבי חייא בר אבא holds that prophecies like "no more war" will literally come true in ימות המשיח, just as the ברייתא assumes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חייא בר אבא, the wonderful prophecies describe ימות המשיח, so the end of war applies then. עולם הבא is so great that no prophet could even describe it. This is the opposite of שמואל's "nothing changes" view.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Chiya bar Abba.
For Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
All the prophets prophesied only
about the days of the Messiah,
but about the World to Come:
"No eye has seen, O God, except You."

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flip side of step 16. The ברייתא opposes שמואל but supports רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר אבא's view that the prophecies apply to ימות המשיח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, where both sides assume weapons will disappear in ימות המשיח

steps.title: A second version: the same challenge to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another version of the ברייתא. The חכמים ask רבי אליעזר the same question as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: They said to רבי אליעזר: Since they are ornaments for him, why will they be eliminated in the days of משיח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the story. The question is word-for-word the same, but רבי אליעזר's answer will be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the question because this is a different version of the conversation. Watch for the change in the answer, since that changes which אמורא the ברייתא matches.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introduces a different version)

phrases.english: And some say:
They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
Since they are ornaments for him,
why will they be eliminated
in the days of the Messiah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the conversation in a different version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that weapons are ornaments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If weapons are ornaments, why would they be removed in a perfect future?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: even in the days of משיח they stay
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי אליעזר answers that weapons will not be removed even in ימות המשיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Even in the days of משיח they will not be eliminated.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר rejects the question's assumption. He says weapons will stay even in ימות המשיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אליעזר does not accept that war will end in ימות המשיח. Since weapons remain, the challenge falls away, and they can still be ornaments.

phrases.english: He said to them: Even in the days of the Messiah
they will not be eliminated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן אַף לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ אֵינָן בְּטֵלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repeated challenge differently from step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weapons will be removed in ימות המשיח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weapons are not removed even in ימות המשיח, so nothing contradicts their being ornaments.

steps.title: The second version matches שמואל and disagrees with רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רבי אליעזר agrees with שמואל and disagrees with רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the view of שמואל, and it disagrees with רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up where the second version stands. The alignments are now reversed from the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If weapons stay in ימות המשיח, the world has not fundamentally changed, which is exactly שמואל's view. It argues with רבי חייא בר אבא, who says the prophecy of no more war applies to ימות המשיח.
steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: weapons are removed in ימות המשיח. This disagrees with שמואל and supports רבי חייא בר אבא. Version 2: weapons are not removed. This matches שמואל and disagrees with רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: A small שבת question about wearing a sword leads into a basic disagreement about what ימות המשיח will look like: a natural world without foreign rule, or the literal fulfillment of the prophecies.

phrases.english: This is the view of Shmuel,
and it disagrees with Rabbi Chiya bar Abba.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי אליעזר's answer in the second version.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two versions of the ברייתא line up with opposite אמוראים: version 1 with רבי חייא בר אבא, version 2 with שמואל.

steps.title: What is the source for calling weapons ornaments?
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב יוסף, depending on the version) asks for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's view that weapons are תכשיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי. Some say he said it to רב אויא. Some say רב יוסף said it to רב דימי. Some say רב יוסף said it to רב אויא. And some say אביי said it to רב יוסף: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר, who said weapons are ornaments for a man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי אליעזר's basic opinion and asks for its source. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned what רבי אליעזר holds: a man may go out on שבת carrying weapons because they are ornaments, not burdens. Now the גמרא wants to know why he thinks a sword counts as an ornament. The long list of names only records the different traditions about who asked whom. It does not change the content of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Ornaments. Things worn as part of one's dress, so they are not a forbidden 'burden' on שבת.
And some say. It introduces another version of who said it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get lost in the list of names. It is one question. The גמרא is only telling you that there were five traditions about which חכם asked it and to whom.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi,
and some say it was to Rav Avya,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב דִּימִי,
phrases.english: and some say Rav Yosef said it to Rav Dimi,
and some say it was to Rav Avya,
and some say Abaye said it to Rav Yosef:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer
who said they are ornaments for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ימות המשיח discussion and returns to the source for רבי אליעזר's basic view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for treating weapons as ornaments.

steps.title: The verse about girding a sword
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק in תהלים that calls a sword 'your glory and your splendor.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one, your glory and your splendor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from תהלים מה:ד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls a sword worn on the thigh 'glory and splendor.' Glory and splendor are words for adornment. So a sword is a form of dress and beauty, not a load being carried.

keyTerms.meaning: Your glory and your splendor, which are words of adornment

phrases.english: As it is written: "Gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one,
your glory and your splendor."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: חֲגוֹר חַרְבְּךָ עַל יָרֵךְ גִּבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תהלים מה:ד calls a sword 'glory and splendor,' so it is an ornament.

steps.title: The verse is about Torah, not swords
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא objects that this פסוק is a metaphor for דברי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to מר בריה דרב הונא: This פסוק is written about words of Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges the proof. He says the פסוק is not talking about real swords at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל explain this פסוק as being about a תלמיד חכם, whose 'sword' is his Torah learning. If the 'sword' is only a picture of Torah, then the פסוק says nothing about real weapons. In that case it cannot prove that weapons are ornaments.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to him,
to Mar, son of Rav Huna:
This verse is written about matters of Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of תהלים מה:ד as a source about real weapons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is understood as a metaphor for Torah, so it cannot teach a law about physical swords.

steps.title: A verse never loses its plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: Even with a Torah metaphor, the plain meaning of the פסוק about a real sword still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A פסוק does not leave its plain meaning.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בריה דרב הונא answers that the metaphor does not cancel the literal meaning. So the proof still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרש about Torah is added on top of the פשט. It does not replace it. The פסוק still also means a real sword, which is called 'glory and splendor.' So it can still prove that weapons are ornaments.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse does not depart from its plain meaning

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the most important rules for reading Torah in all of תלמוד and in the מפרשים. A דרש can add meaning, but it never wipes out the פשט.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A verse does not depart from its literal meaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the proof against רב כהנא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Interpretive principle: the פשט stays alongside the דרש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסוק is a metaphor for Torah, its literal meaning drops away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The literal meaning stays in force, so the פסוק proves that a sword is an ornament.

steps.title: רב כהנא only learned this rule late
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that he had learned all of תלמוד by eighteen, yet did not know this rule until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: When I was eighteen years old, I had already learned the whole תלמוד. Yet I did not know that a פסוק does not leave its plain meaning until now.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא shares a personal comment about how surprised he was by this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He had learned a huge amount at a young age. Even so, this basic rule of reading only became clear to him much later. The comment sets up the question in the next step: why does the גמרא record it?

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: כַּד הֲוֵינָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנִין
phrases.english: When I was eighteen years old
and had learned the entire Talmud,
and I did not know
that a verse does not depart from its literal meaning
until now.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּד הֲוֵינָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב כהנא reacts personally to the rule taught in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even someone who had mastered all of תלמוד could miss this basic rule until later in life.

steps.title: What is the lesson of רב כהנא's story?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we are meant to learn from רב כהנא's remark.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב כהנא's personal remark matters. This is a setup for the lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that a recorded statement must teach something. So it asks what practical lesson comes out of רב כהנא's confession.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the point of step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lesson of רב כהנא's statement.

steps.title: First learn, then understand
steps.stepSummary: A person should first learn the material and only afterward work to understand it deeply.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a person should first learn, and afterward reason it through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the lesson: build broad knowledge first, and deep understanding will come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא knew all of תלמוד before he understood this basic rule. His story shows that wide learning comes first, and understanding grows with time. So a learner should not hold back from learning just because he does not yet understand everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Should learn (gain knowledge of the material)
Should understand or reason it out

steps.whatToRemember: Two lasting lessons: (1) אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו, meaning a פסוק keeps its plain meaning even when it also has a דרש. (2) דליגמר איניש והדר ליסבר, meaning first learn, then understand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic guide for how to learn. Cover the material first, and the depth will come.

phrases.english: That a person should learn
and afterward understand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.

steps.title: Memory aid for the next teachings
steps.stepSummary: The word 'זרות' is a סימן (memory aid) for the אמוראים whose teachings on this פסוק come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: 'זרות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory aid that sets up the next group of teachings. The next part explains the following פסוק in the same מזמור (תהלים מה:ה) as being about Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation is that the letters stand for רבי אלעזר (ז), ריש לקיש (ר), and their students (ו, ת). רבי אלעזר's teaching expounds the next פסוק in תהלים מה. The teachings of ריש לקיש that follow use other פסוקים (מלאכי, שיר השירים) on the same theme of scholars learning together. The סימן helps the learner remember the order of the statements that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The code word whose letters stand for the coming speakers

phrases.english: Mnemonic: "Zarot."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition that opens a new section of teachings on the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid listing the speakers of the coming teachings.

steps.title: Scholars who sharpen each other are given success
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes רבי אלעזר: when two תלמידי חכמים sharpen each other in הלכה, הקב״ה gives them success. The source is the פסוק 'והדרך צלח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי אלעזר: When two תלמידי חכמים sharpen each other in הלכה, הקב״ה makes them succeed, as the verse says: 'And in your majesty, prosper.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first of the teachings on this פסוק, the ones that the סימן 'זרות' pointed to. רבי אלעזר says that scholars who sharpen each other will succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that sharp back-and-forth learning between two people brings Divine success. Right now the פסוק seems to say only 'majesty' and 'prosper.' The very next step shows how the word 'majesty' is read as 'sharpening.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Two Torah scholars
who sharpen one another in halacha,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes them succeed,
as it is said: 'And in your majesty, prosper.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the teachings that the סימן 'זרות' in step 28 was pointing to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two scholars who sharpen each other in הלכה are given success by הקב״ה.

steps.title: Reading 'your majesty' as 'your sharpening'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'והדרך' (your majesty) is re-read as 'וחדדך' (your sharpening). This ties the פסוק to sharp learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read it as 'and your majesty' (וַהֲדָרְךָ). Read it instead as 'and your sharpening' (וַחֲדָדְךָ).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the פסוק proves רבי אלעזר's teaching. It changes how one word is read so that the word means 'sharpening.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By swapping the ה for a ח and the ר for a ד, 'majesty' becomes 'sharpening.' So the פסוק now says 'your sharpening will succeed,' which matches the teaching exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not read it as...': a דרשה that re-reads a word

steps.confusionAlert: An 'אל תקרי' does not change the actual text of the פסוק. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of the simple reading.

phrases.english: Do not read: 'and your majesty,'
but rather 'and your sharpening.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 29 actually supports the teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That sharpening each other brings success.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The re-reading of 'והדרך' as 'וחדדך' in תהלים מ״ה:ה.

steps.title: They also rise to greatness
steps.stepSummary: Beyond success, such scholars rise to high positions. The source is 'צלח רכב' (prosper, ride on).
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but they rise to greatness, as it is said: 'Prosper, ride on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reward for scholars who sharpen each other: they rise to greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Riding' is a picture of high status, like a ruler riding a chariot. So the next words of the פסוק add greatness on top of success.

keyTerms.meaning: and not only that, but also

phrases.english: And not only that, but they rise to greatness,
as it is said: 'Prosper, ride on.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further reward, drawn from the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars who sharpen each other also rise to greatness.

steps.title: Only if they learn for the right reasons
steps.stepSummary: One might think the reward comes even when learning שלא לשמה. The words 'על דבר אמת' teach that it must be for the sake of truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think this applies even when they learn not for its own sake. Therefore the verse says: 'On behalf of truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the reward. It raises a possible mistake ("maybe even without pure motives") and corrects it from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'יכול... תלמוד לומר' pattern suggests a possible wrong idea and then blocks it. The words 'for the sake of truth' show that the success comes only to those who learn לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought...' (raising a possible mistake)
not for its own sake (with other motives)
'therefore the verse says': the correction from the פסוק

phrases.english: I might have thought: even not for its own sake.
Therefore the verse says: 'On behalf of truth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rewards from steps 29 and 31 to those who learn לשמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward applies only to learning for the sake of truth (לשמה).

steps.title: Only if they stay humble
steps.stepSummary: One might think the reward comes even to someone who became arrogant. The words 'וענוה צדק' teach that humility is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think this applies even if he became arrogant. Therefore the verse says: 'Humility and righteousness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit with the same pattern: arrogance cancels the reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next words of the פסוק, 'humility, righteousness,' teach that a sharp scholar who becomes proud loses the promised success. So the reward needs pure motives and humility together.

phrases.english: I might have thought: even if he became arrogant.
Therefore the verse says: 'Humility and righteousness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second limit, built the same way as step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An arrogant scholar does not get the promised reward. Humility is required.

steps.title: They merit the Torah given with the right hand
steps.stepSummary: If they learn this proper way, they merit the Torah that was given with הקב״ה's right hand, as the פסוק ends 'ותורך נוראות ימינך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they do so, they merit the Torah that was given with the right hand, as it is said: 'And your right hand will teach you awesome things.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר's teaching with the final reward for learning properly: the Torah 'of the right hand.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק mentions the 'right hand.' רבי אלעזר reads this as the Torah given from הקב״ה's right hand. What exactly 'right hand' means here is explained differently in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: sharpening each other brings success and greatness, but only with pure motives (לשמה) and humility. Then they merit the Torah of the 'right hand.'

phrases.english: And if they do so,
they merit the Torah that was given with the right hand,
as it is said: 'And your right hand will teach you awesome things.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final reward once the conditions of steps 32 and 33 are met.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who learn properly merit the Torah given with the right hand.

steps.title: Another reading: the blessings on Torah's right side
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the 'right hand' differently: they merit the blessings that are described as being in the Torah's right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They merit the things that were said about the right hand of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different explanation of the reward. It is not the Torah from ה׳'s right hand, but the blessings in the Torah's own right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב נחמן בר יצחק's view, 'right hand' points to a different פסוק that describes what the Torah holds in her right hand. The next steps bring that פסוק and explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: in the right hand of the Torah

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They merit the things that were said
about the right hand of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the 'right hand' reward from step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward is the blessings described as being in the Torah's right hand.

steps.title: What does the verse about the Torah's two hands mean?
steps.stepSummary: To back up רב נחמן בר יצחק, the גמרא quotes רב ששת (the chain of names is disputed), who asks about the meaning of 'אורך ימים בימינה בשמאלה עושר וכבוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא בר רב שילא said, and some say רב יוסף בר חמא said, in the name of רב ששת: What is the meaning of the verse 'Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are wealth and honor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that רב נחמן בר יצחק was pointing to. It sets up a question about what the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who passed on רב ששת's teaching. The question 'מאי דכתיב' introduces a problem with the פסוק, and that problem is stated in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (another version of who said it)
what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: As Rava bar Rav Sheila said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא
phrases.english: and some say Rav Yosef bar Chama said
that Rav Sheshet said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'Long life is in her right hand;
in her left hand are wealth and honor'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק (משלי ג:טז) behind רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the פסוק that splits long life from wealth and honor between the Torah's hands.

steps.title: Does the right hand lack wealth and honor?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges the simple reading: could it be that the right side, the better side, has long life but no wealth and honor?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it that in her right hand there is long life, and there is no wealth and honor?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת points out the problem with reading the פסוק simply. The 'better' right hand seems to be missing wealth and honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the right side is the more important one. So it makes no sense for the right side to have less than the left side. That pushes us toward a different reading.

phrases.english: But in her right hand is there long life,
and there is no wealth and honor?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the difficulty that the question in step 36 was pointing to.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of משלי ג:טז.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The more important right side cannot logically have fewer blessings than the left side.

steps.title: Learning 'with the right' versus 'with the left'
steps.stepSummary: The 'right' and 'left' describe two kinds of learners. Those who learn properly ('right') get long life and surely wealth and honor. Those who learn improperly ('left') get wealth and honor, but not long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: For those who use their right hand with it, there is long life, and all the more so wealth and honor. For those who use their left hand with it, there is wealth and honor, but no long life.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers by saying the hands stand for the way a person learns, not for the Torah's own hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning 'with the right hand' means learning skillfully and with the right intentions (לשמה). Those learners get everything. Learners who use the weaker 'left hand' get only wealth and honor. This explains רב נחמן בר יצחק: proper learners earn the 'right side' blessings, the full package.

keyTerms.meaning: those who use the 'right hand' in it (learn properly, לשמה)
those who use the 'left hand' in it (learn improperly)

steps.whatToRemember: Learning Torah the proper way brings long life plus wealth and honor. Learning it the improper way may bring wealth and honor, but not long life.

phrases.english: Rather: for those who use their right hand with it,
there is long life,
and all the more so wealth and honor.
For those who use their left hand with it,
there is wealth and honor,
but there is no long life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of step 37 with a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading: 'right' and 'left' describe the learner's approach, not the Torah's hands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The right hand holds only long life, and the left hand holds only wealth and honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proper learners get long life and all the more so wealth and honor. Improper learners get only wealth and honor.

steps.title: ה׳ listens to scholars who are gentle with each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes ריש לקיש: when two תלמידי חכמים are pleasant to each other in learning, הקב״ה listens to them, based on 'אז נדברו יראי ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: When two תלמידי חכמים are pleasant to each other in הלכה, הקב״ה listens to them, as it is said: 'Then those who feared ה׳ spoke with one another...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next teaching in the series. Scholars who discuss הלכה calmly and pleasantly get ה׳'s attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the praise was for sharpness. Here the praise is for gentleness. The פסוק in מלאכי continues 'and ה׳ listened and heard.' The next step explains why 'נדברו' means calm, pleasant speech.

keyTerms.meaning: who are pleasant, agreeable to each other

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Two Torah scholars
who are pleasant to each other in halacha,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, listens to them,
as it is said: 'Then those who feared ה׳ spoke with one another, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the 'זרות' series, parallel to רבי אלעזר's in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two scholars who are gentle with each other in הלכה are listened to by הקב״ה.

steps.title: The word 'דיבור' means calm
steps.stepSummary: The proof that 'נדברו' means gentle speech: 'דיבור' means calm, as in 'ידבר עמים תחתינו' (He brings nations calmly under us).
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'speech' (דִּבּוּר) means nothing other than calm, as it is said: 'He subdues (יַדְבֵּר) peoples under us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from another פסוק that the root 'דבר' can mean calm and settled. So 'נדברו' describes a calm, pleasant conversation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תהלים מ״ז, 'ידבר' describes nations quietly brought under Israel, which is a state of calm. Using that same meaning, 'נדברו' in מלאכי means the scholars spoke peacefully.
steps.confusionAlert: Usually 'דיבור' can mean harsh speech. Here the גמרא deliberately reads it as calm, based on the פסוק 'ידבר עמים'.

phrases.english: 'Speech' means nothing other than calm,
as it is said: 'He subdues peoples under us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the meaning of 'נדברו' used in step 39.
steps.raayaObject: That 'נדברו' refers to calm, pleasant speech.

steps.title: What does 'those who think of His name' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the end of the same פסוק in מלאכי: 'ולחושבי שמו' (and for those who think of His name).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and for those who think of His name'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another phrase in the same פסוק and asks what it means. This sets up רבי אמי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists 'those who fear ה׳' and also 'those who think of His name.' The second phrase seems to describe a separate group, so the גמרא asks who they are.

keyTerms.meaning: and for those who think of His name

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'and for those who think of His name'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about another phrase in the פסוק quoted in step 39.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is meant by 'those who think of His name.'

steps.title: Planning a מצוה counts as doing it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי: if someone planned to do a מצוה but was prevented by circumstances beyond his control (אונס), the פסוק credits him as if he did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Even if a person planned to do a מצוה, and was forced by circumstances and did not do it, the verse credits him as if he had done it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that 'those who think of His name' are people who planned a מצוה but could not do it. They get full credit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Thinking' here means planning. The person really wanted to do the מצוה and was stopped only by an אונס, something outside his control. So his plan is written in the 'book of remembrance' as though he did the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: as if he had done it

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who sincerely plans a מצוה and is prevented by אונס gets credit as if he did it.
steps.confusionAlert: This applies only when the person was truly prevented (נאנס). It does not apply when he simply changed his mind or was lazy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Even if he planned to do a מצוה,
and was prevented by circumstances and did not do it,
the verse credits him as if he had done it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Those who think of His name' are people who planned a מצוה but were prevented by אונס. They are credited as if they did it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle: מחשבה טובה (a good intention) that was blocked by אונס is counted as a completed מצוה.

steps.title: Doing a מצוה properly protects from bad news
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר אידי teaches that whoever does a מצוה exactly as commanded will not hear bad news, based on the פסוק 'שומר מצוה לא ידע דבר רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר אידי said: Anyone who does a מצוה the way it was commanded will not be told bad news, as the פסוק says: 'One who keeps a מצוה will not know a bad thing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that praises people who do מצוות carefully and properly. Their reward is that bad news will not reach them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'כמאמרה', meaning doing the מצוה exactly as it was commanded, with care for every detail. The proof is a פסוק in קהלת. רב חיננא reads 'לא ידע דבר רע' (will not know a bad thing) to mean that such a person will not even be told bad news.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was commanded; done exactly the right way
One who keeps or guards a מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Chinena bar Idi said:
Anyone who does a מצוה as it was commanded
they do not tell him bad news,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שׁוֹמֵר מִצְוָה לֹא יֵדַע דָּבָר רָע״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'One who keeps a מצוה will not know a bad thing' (Koheles 8:5).
phrases.notes: The source for the reward of hearing no bad news.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר אִידִי: כָּל הָעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה כְּמַאֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme from step 42 about the reward for מצוות. There the reward was for planning a מצוה; here it is for doing it properly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who does a מצוה exactly as commanded will not be told bad news (שומר מצוה לא ידע דבר רע).

steps.title: Even a heavenly decree can be cancelled for one who keeps מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי (or רבי חנינא) teaches that even when הקב״ה issues a decree, it can be cancelled. He learns this because the פסוק about the King's unstoppable word sits right next to 'שומר מצוה לא ידע דבר רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said, and some say it was רבי חנינא: Even if הקב״ה makes a decree, it can be cancelled. As the פסוק says: 'For the word of the King has power, and who can say to Him, What are You doing?' And right next to it is written: 'One who keeps a מצוה will not know a bad thing.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching builds on the same פסוק from קהלת. It goes further: for someone who keeps מצוות, even a decree from Heaven can be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the King's word is so powerful that no one can question it. Yet the very next פסוק says the one who keeps מצוות will know no evil. Placing them side by side (סמיכות) teaches that even this powerful decree can be cancelled for the sake of the שומר מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say; another version of who said it
Placed right next to it; the next פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the first פסוק alone proves the point. On its own it says the opposite: no one can stop the King's word. The proof comes only from reading it together with the next פסוק about the שומר מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said, and some say it was Rabbi Chanina:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹזֵר גְּזֵירָה —
phrases.english: Even if the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes a decree,
it gets cancelled,
phrases.notes: Literally 'he cancels it': either הקב״ה cancels it, or the person keeping the מצוה causes it to be cancelled.

phrases.english: as it says: 'For the word of the King has power,
and who can say to Him: What are You doing?' (Koheles 8:4),
and right next to it is written:
'One who keeps a מצוה will not know a bad thing' (Koheles 8:5).
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים side by side teach that the decree is cancelled for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֲפִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹזֵר גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק as step 43 but adds a bigger reward: even a heavenly decree can be cancelled, not just bad news avoided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a decree from הקב״ה can be cancelled for one who keeps מצוות, learned from the two פסוקים placed side by side in קהלת 8:4-5.

steps.title: ה׳ listens to scholars who listen to each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא, quoting ריש לקיש, teaches that when two תלמידי חכמים listen carefully to each other in הלכה, הקב״ה listens to their voice, based on a פסוק in שיר השירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: Two תלמידי חכמים who listen to each other in הלכה, הקב״ה listens to their voice, as the פסוק says: 'You who sit in the gardens, the friends listen to your voice, let Me hear it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from ריש לקיש about how two scholars should learn together. If they truly listen to each other, הקב״ה listens to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is close to the teaching in step 39, which was about scholars being pleasant to each other. Here the focus is on really listening (מקשיבים) to the other person's words in הלכה. The פסוק describes 'friends' who listen, and then God says 'let Me hear it,' showing that He joins in and listens.

keyTerms.meaning: You who sit in the gardens; read here as those sitting and learning

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Two Torah scholars
who listen carefully to each other in halacha,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, listens to their voice,
as it says: 'You who sit in the gardens,
the friends listen to your voice, let Me hear it' (Shir HaShirim 8:13).
phrases.notes: The friends listen to each other, and God asks to hear them too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמַּקְשִׁיבִים זֶה לָזֶה בַּהֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of step 39 (ריש לקיש on scholars learning together), now with a different פסוק and a focus on listening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two תלמידי חכמים truly listen to each other in הלכה, הקב״ה listens to their voice.

steps.title: Not listening to each other drives the שכינה away
steps.stepSummary: The other side of ריש לקיש's teaching: if scholars do not listen to each other, they cause the שכינה to leave ישראל, based on the next פסוק, 'ברח דודי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they do not do this, they cause the שכינה to leave ישראל, as the פסוק says: 'Run away, my Beloved, and be like a gazelle...'
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes ריש לקיש's teaching by giving the opposite case. Scholars who do not listen to each other push the שכינה away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the very next פסוק in שיר השירים, right after 'let Me hear it.' If the friends do not listen to each other, God does not stay to listen. Instead He 'runs away,' which shows the שכינה leaving. Listening brings God close, and not listening sends Him away.
steps.whatToRemember: Two scholars who listen to each other bring הקב״ה close: He listens to them. Scholars who do not listen to each other cause the שכינה to leave ישראל. The way we learn together matters, not only what we learn.

phrases.english: And if they do not do this,
phrases.notes: That is, if they do not listen to each other.

phrases.english: they cause the Shechinah to leave Israel,
as it says: 'Run away, my Beloved, and be like (a gazelle)...' (Shir HaShirim 8:14).
phrases.notes: This פסוק comes right after the one in the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 45 by giving the opposite outcome, proven from the very next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars who do not listen to each other cause the שכינה to leave ישראל.

steps.title: God loves two scholars who learn together, even when they make mistakes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא, quoting ריש לקיש, teaches that two תלמידי חכמים who are מדגילים each other in הלכה are loved by הקב״ה. He learns this from the פסוק 'ודגלו עלי אהבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: Two תלמידי חכמים who lead each other into mistakes in הלכה while learning together are still loved by הקב״ה. As the verse says: 'And his banner over me is love.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of ריש לקיש about two scholars who learn together. Even when their joint learning leads them into mistakes, הקב״ה loves them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a wordplay: הַמַּדְגִּילִים (leading astray) sounds like וְדִגְלוֹ (his banner) in the פסוק. The idea is that God loves the effort of learning together, even when the result is not perfect. This differs from the teaching in Step 45: there, the scholars listen to each other; here, the scholars are loved even though they err.

keyTerms.meaning: Lead each other into error (תוספות); רש״י explains it as sharpening each other
'And his banner over me is love' (שיר השירים 2:4)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 45. That teaching was about scholars who listen to each other (מקשיבים). This one is about scholars who are מדגילים each other, which is a separate statement from the same חכם.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Two Torah scholars
who cause one another to err in halacha
phrases.notes: This line follows תוספות. רש״י reads it as a good thing: they 'raise the banner,' sharpening each other.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves them,
as it is stated: 'And his banner over me is love.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ריש לקיש teaching about scholars learning together, following the pair in Steps 45-46.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two scholars who lead each other into error in their learning are still loved by הקב״ה (from 'ודגלו עלי אהבה').

steps.title: רבא limits the teaching with two conditions
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the love described in Step 47 applies only when (1) the scholars already know the basic structure of the law, and (2) there is no great teacher in their town they could learn from instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This applies only when they know the basic outline of the teaching. And it applies only when there is no great teacher in the town for them to learn from.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows ריש לקיש's teaching. Not every pair of learners who make mistakes earns this praise, only those who meet two conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Condition one: they know the צורתא דשמעתא, the basic foundation. So their mistakes come from missing finer details, not from complete ignorance. Condition two: there is no רבה in town. If a real teacher were available, learning alone and making mistakes would not be praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And that is only when…', a phrase that adds a limiting condition
The basic shape or foundation of the teaching
A great teacher in the town

steps.whatToRemember: God loves two scholars who learn together and stumble, as long as they know the basics and have no great teacher available to learn from.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And that is only where they know the foundation of the law.
And that is only where they do not have a great teacher in the city
to learn from.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְהוּא דְּיָדְעִי צוּרְתָּא דִשְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two limiting conditions to ריש לקיש's statement in Step 47.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The praise applies only when the scholars know the basics and have no great teacher available.

steps.title: Lending is greater than charity, and partnership is greatest of all
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, via רבי אבא, ranks three ways of helping someone: a loan is greater than צדקה, and going into partnership with him is greatest of all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: One who lends money is greater than one who gives צדקה. And one who puts money into a shared purse with the poor person is greater than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ריש לקיש teaching on a new topic. It ranks the ways of helping a needy person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ranking follows how much the poor person's dignity is protected. With a loan, he is not taking a handout. With a partnership (מטיל בכיס), he looks like an equal business partner, so he feels no shame at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts money into a shared purse, meaning he enters a business partnership with the needy person

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a classic source for the idea that the highest form of צדקה helps a person stand on his own without embarrassment.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Greater is one who lends
than one who gives charity.
And one who places money into a shared purse is greatest of them all.
phrases.notes: This means a partnership with the poor person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: גָּדוֹל הַמַּלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching in the same chain of ריש לקיש statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan is greater than צדקה, and a partnership is greatest of all.

steps.title: Stay close to a scholar even if he is hard; avoid living near an ignorant pious man
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a תלמיד חכם should be kept close even if he is vengeful like a snake. But one should not live in the neighborhood of an עם הארץ, even a pious one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: Even if a תלמיד חכם takes revenge and holds grudges like a snake, wrap him around your waist. Even if an עם הארץ is a חסיד, do not live in his neighborhood.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ריש לקיש teaching, this time about which people to keep near you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The value of a scholar's Torah outweighs his difficult character, so stay close to him and benefit from what he knows. A pious person who lacks Torah knowledge may act wrongly while thinking he is right, and you may copy him. Torah knowledge is presented as the deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes revenge and holds a grudge
Wrap him around your waist, meaning keep him close

steps.confusionAlert: This is not praising revenge. The point is that the scholar's Torah is worth staying close to, despite his flaw.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
If a Torah scholar
is vengeful and holds grudges like a snake,
wrap him around your waist.
If an ignorant person is pious,
do not live in his neighborhood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next teaching in the chain of ריש לקיש statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep a תלמיד חכם close despite his hard nature; do not live near even a pious עם הארץ.

steps.title: Keeping a vicious dog keeps kindness out of the home
steps.stepSummary: Reported in three possible chains of names, ריש לקיש teaches that whoever raises a dangerous dog at home keeps חסד away from his house. He begins quoting a פסוק that starts with 'למס'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש (some say רב אסי said it in the name of ריש לקיש, and some say רבי אבא said it in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש): Anyone who raises a vicious dog in his home holds back חסד from his home, as the verse says: 'To him that is afflicted…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ריש לקיש teaching and notes three different versions of who reported it. It starts quoting the supporting פסוק, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Poor people are afraid to come to a house with a vicious dog, so the owner loses chances to do חסד. The three 'ואמרי לה' lines record disagreement about who passed the teaching on. The teaching itself is the same in all three versions. The proof from 'למס' is only begun here and will be explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say it…', introducing a different chain of names for the same teaching
'To the afflicted one' (start of the פסוק in איוב 6:14)

steps.confusionAlert: The three 'ואמרי לה' versions are not three different opinions. They are three possible lists of who reported the same teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
